name: Polygenic Score (PGS) Catalog
maintainer: EMBL-EBI (with the NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog team and the University of Cambridge)
scope: Published polygenic score models: one scoring file of variant weights per score, with the publication, the trait, how the score was developed, the samples and cohorts used, and its reported performance in evaluation samples.
mapping_methods: Scoring files are author-reported; harmonised versions add chromosome and position by rsID lookup or lift-over and flag problematic variants (palindromic SNPs, strand flips, variants absent from the Ensembl variation databases). Ensembl version 105 is used for the rsID to position mapping.

quantitative.summary: Per-variant effect weights (log odds ratios, betas or other, as the scoring file states), and per-score performance metrics (AUROC, OR, HR, R2) in evaluation samples with their confidence intervals.
quantitative.units: weight type given per score in the file header; not always reported
quantitative.uncertainty: Performance metrics carry confidence intervals; individual weights carry none.

licence.name: EMBL-EBI terms of use by default; a scoring file's own licence field governs that score and can be more restrictive (for example CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 for scores from Ambry Genetics)

update_frequency: Frequent (new scores are curated from a weekly literature search; metadata files are re-released with each update).
coverage_limitations: A score is a model of many weights for one trait, not evidence about any single variant; it is built and evaluated mostly in cohorts of European ancestry, and performance does not transfer unchanged to other ancestries.
Scoring files are consistently formatted but author-reported; the harmonised GRCh38 file exists only where harmonisation succeeded.
known_omissions: No reference score distributions are provided, so a raw score cannot be turned into a percentile without a reference panel in the same ancestry.

reuse_decision.rationale: The bulk metadata (scores, publications, traits, samples, cohorts, performance) is small and is the registry of models; the harmonised GRCh38 scoring files are retrieved for a documented selection and applied to a sample by a separate scoring step. Scores are not merged into the variant evidence index: a polygenic score is a model, not an assertion about a variant.

status.notes: FTP listing, bulk metadata files and the harmonised file for the first score were read; the web pages were read in a plain request.

evidence_profile.biological_context: Each score is a weighted sum of effect-allele dosages from a published model, developed for a stated trait in stated development samples and evaluated in other samples; ancestry and cohort come with the score.
evidence_profile.evidence_strength: Reported performance of the score as a whole in its evaluation samples. A single weight is an association estimate for one allele in a model and carries no individual evidence strength.
evidence_profile.mechanistic_confidence: None. Weights are statistical effect estimates in a prediction model; they identify neither causal variants nor mechanisms.
evidence_profile.phenotype_implication: Predisposition to a trait in the ancestry the score was developed and evaluated in. A raw score is meaningful only against a reference distribution of the same score and ancestry.
evidence_profile.absence_means: A variant that is not a weight of a score was not selected or estimated by that model. Absence from a score is not evidence of no effect, and a missing genotype is not a zero dosage.

overlaps_with_sources.note: scores are developed from genome-wide association results, which may or may not be among the GWAS Catalog studies; compare, do not pool
